name: Hawaii
hook: The 50th state in six moves: islands, volcanoes, Kamehameha and the words visitors take home.

facts.label: the Big Island
facts.statement: Hawaii is the largest island in the United States — hence its nickname, the Big Island — and it holds Mauna Loa, the largest volcano on Earth.

facts.label: Maui
facts.statement: Maui is the second-largest Hawaiian island, the "Valley Isle," home to Haleakala National Park and Maui Gold pineapple.

facts.label: Oahu
facts.statement: Oahu is the third-largest island in the chain, home to the NFL Pro Bowl and the National Memorial Cemetery of the Pacific in Punchbowl Crater.

facts.label: Kauai
facts.statement: Kauai is the "Garden Isle"; Mount Waialeale there is one of the wettest places on Earth, averaging about 450 inches of rain a year.

facts.label: Kamehameha
facts.statement: Kamehameha I unified the Hawaiian Islands and built the Pu'ukohola Heiau; his yellow feather cloak is at the Bishop Museum.

facts.label: the ukulele
facts.statement: The ukulele, derived from the Portuguese machete, is Hawaii's official modern instrument and is tuned with the ditty "My Dog Has Fleas."

facts.label: aloha
facts.statement: Aloha means both hello and goodbye, and gave its name to the aloha shirt Truman wore on a 1951 Life cover.
